high.title: Peso May Stay at P61:$1 Level
high.summary: The Philippine Peso staged a notable recovery on Friday, surging 32 centavos to close at P61.24 against the USD from P61.56 on Thursday — its strongest finish in over a month since June 29's P61.17 close. Market participants expect the Peso to continue trading sideways within the P61 range in the near term, with direction hinging on two key drivers: global oil price movements and the upcoming release of critical Philippine economic data (likely July CPI). For FX traders, the P61 level represents a key technical and psychological support/resistance zone. A softer-than-expected CPI print could catalyze further Peso appreciation by reducing pressure on the BSP to maintain a hawkish stance, while an upside inflation surprise could push USD/PHP back toward the P61.50–P62.00 range. Traders should monitor oil price volatility closely, as the Philippines is a net oil importer, making the current account sensitive to energy price swings. **Watch:** July CPI release and Fed commentary for next directional catalyst.

high.title: T-Bill and Bond Rates May Be Mixed Before CPI Data
high.summary: Philippine government securities rates are expected to trade mixed this week ahead of key domestic economic data, with renewed inflation concerns reinforcing a cautious market tone. The Bureau of the Treasury (BTr) will auction P50 billion in T-bills on Monday — P20 billion each in 91- and 182-day papers and P10 billion in 364-day notes — followed by a P30 billion reissuance of T-bonds on Tuesday. For bond investors, the mixed rate outlook reflects a market in a wait-and-see mode: if July CPI surprises to the upside, yields could rise sharply as BSP rate cut expectations get pushed further out. Conversely, benign inflation could trigger a rally across the curve. **Key risk:** A hawkish Fed posture continuing to anchor the short end of the Philippine yield curve higher. Investors should watch auction bid-to-cover ratios as a sentiment gauge ahead of the CPI print.

high.title: Government Debt Yields Slip as Players Turn Defensive Amid Volatility
high.summary: Philippine government securities (GS) yields closed mostly lower last week, declining an average of 2.33 basis points week-on-week based on PHP Bloomberg Valuation Service (BVAL) Reference Rates as of July 31. The short end of the curve led the move, with 91- and 364-day T-bill rates falling 3.63 bps, reflecting defensive positioning amid volatile oil prices and a hawkish-pause stance from the US Federal Reserve. The yield decline implies modest price appreciation in GS, suggesting some safe-haven demand for Philippine government paper despite external headwinds. For bond investors, the defensive tone signals that market participants are not yet pricing in aggressive BSP easing — they are holding duration cautiously rather than extending it. The Fed's "hawkish pause" dynamic is critically important: it limits the BSP's room to cut rates without risking capital outflows and Peso depreciation pressure. **Watch:** Whether the yield rally extends post-CPI data, and whether the BTr's upcoming auctions are met with strong demand or undersubscription, which would reveal true investor risk appetite.

high.title: Poll: Philippine Inflation Steady at 6.4% in July
high.summary: Philippine headline inflation is forecast to have held at 6.4% in July — matching June's reading but dramatically elevated versus the 0.9% print from a year earlier, according to a BusinessWorld poll of 21 economists. This would mark the **fifth consecutive month** of inflation breaching the BSP's 4% upper target ceiling. Lower food prices, particularly rice, are seen as the key offsetting factor against higher fuel and electricity costs. For FX and rates traders, persistently above-target inflation significantly constrains the BSP's ability to cut its policy rate, even as economic growth appears to be slowing (see GDP article below). This stagflationary backdrop is PHP-negative in the near term — elevated rates may support the currency partially, but weakening growth erodes investor confidence. Bond investors should remain cautious on duration, as the BSP is unlikely to pivot dovish with inflation this far above target. **Key event to watch:** Official July CPI release from PSA, which will confirm or revise market expectations.

high.title: Q2 GDP Growth Likely Slowed to 2.8% — Poll
high.summary: The Philippine economy is forecast to have expanded by only **2.8% year-on-year in Q2 2026**, according to a BusinessWorld poll of 21 economists — a marked deceleration from recent quarters. The slowdown is attributed to elevated inflation eroding household purchasing power, weakening business confidence, and sluggish public infrastructure disbursements. For macro traders, a 2.8% print would represent a significant growth disappointment and compounds the bearish narrative alongside sticky high inflation — a classic stagflation scenario. This puts the BSP in a difficult position: cutting rates risks exacerbating inflation and PHP weakness, while holding rates tight prolongs the growth squeeze. Philippine government bond yields could come under upward pressure if markets price in a prolonged high-rate environment, while the PSEi faces headwinds from weaker corporate earnings visibility. **Key event to watch:** Official Q2 GDP release from PSA; any print below 2.8% would likely trigger a PHP sell-off and PSEi downside.

high.title: Cautious Trading Likely Before Inflation and GDP Data
high.summary: The PSEi fell **1.09% (–69.31 points) to close at 6,236.44** on Friday — its worst close in recent sessions — with the broader All Shares Index also declining 0.59% to 3,395.05. Market sentiment is expected to remain subdued this week as investors adopt a wait-and-see stance ahead of the official July inflation and Q2 GDP data releases. Middle East geopolitical tensions are cited as an additional risk-off factor weighing on sentiment. For equity traders, the index is at a technically fragile level; a GDP miss or inflation surprise to the upside could push PSEi toward key support levels below 6,200. Foreign fund flows will be critical to monitor — risk-off global conditions combined with domestic macro weakness could accelerate net foreign selling on the exchange, adding further PHP depreciation pressure through equity-related capital outflows.

high.title: Peso Up on Yen Intervention, Middle East Peace Deal Hopes
high.summary: The Philippine Peso staged a notable recovery on Monday, surging 31 centavos to close at P60.93 per dollar — its strongest finish in over six weeks — from Friday's close of P61.24. The rally was driven by two key catalysts: (1) a recovery in the Japanese yen following coordinated intervention by Japanese and U.S. regulators, which broadly weakened the dollar across Asian FX markets, and (2) easing geopolitical tensions in the Middle East, which improved global risk sentiment. For FX traders, the return toward the P60-handle is technically significant, suggesting near-term support at current levels. However, the move appears externally driven rather than underpinned by domestic fundamentals. Traders should monitor the durability of the yen intervention effect and any reversal in Middle East headlines, as these could quickly unwind gains. The peso remains structurally pressured above P60 (see Metrobank outlook), meaning this bounce may represent a tactical opportunity rather than a trend reversal. Watch for BSP commentary on FX conditions and any signs of reserve deployment.

high.title: Peso to Stay Above P60 Until 2027 on Dollar's Strength, Weak Growth
high.summary: Metrobank Research Officer Sophia Therese Bonifacio, in a July 30 commentary, projects the Philippine Peso will remain above the P60-per-dollar level through end-2027, citing persistent domestic and external headwinds. Key pressures include tight domestic economic conditions, continued USD strength, and weak growth dynamics. Importantly, Metrobank flags that anticipated BSP monetary policy easing — once inflation pressures recede — could serve as an additional headwind for the peso, as rate cuts would narrow the interest rate differential with the USD. For bond investors, this outlook suggests that any BSP easing cycle could be gradual and data-dependent, with FX stability considerations acting as a binding constraint on the pace of cuts. For FX traders, the structural bearish bias on PHP/USD remains intact despite Monday's tactical bounce. The P60 level is a critical psychological threshold, and a sustained break below it appears unlikely until 2027 under this base case. Portfolio managers should factor prolonged peso weakness into hedging strategies and return assumptions for Philippine asset allocations.

high.title: T-Bill Yields Decline on Iran Deal Hopes
high.summary: The Bureau of the Treasury (BTr) achieved a full award of P50 billion in T-bills at Monday's auction, with rates declining across all tenors amid improved global risk sentiment tied to easing U.S.-Iran tensions and falling global oil prices. Demand was exceptionally strong — total tenders reached P167.742 billion, more than three times the offered amount and significantly above last week's P134.519 billion in bids. For bond investors, the robust bid-to-cover ratio and lower clearing yields signal strong appetite for short-duration Philippine government paper, likely reflecting both domestic liquidity conditions and a risk-on shift in sentiment. The oil price angle is particularly relevant: lower crude prices reduce imported inflation pressures, potentially giving the BSP more room to ease policy rates — a bullish signal for the broader bond market. Traders should watch whether the yield decline extends to longer-tenor GS instruments at upcoming auctions, which would confirm a broader bond market rally. The strong overbid also reduces near-term rollover risk for the government's borrowing program.

high.title: Japan, US Confirm Joint Yen-Buying Intervention, Signal Further Action
high.summary:
A rare and significant bilateral coordination between Japan and the United States to conduct yen-buying FX intervention has been confirmed by Japan's Ministry of Finance. The joint action was triggered by the yen's slide to fresh 40-year lows, with both governments signaling readiness for further intervention. Analysts highlight that the sell-off in both the yen and Japanese Government Bonds (JGBs) risked generating adverse global spillovers, most notably upward pressure on already elevated US Treasury yields.

For PHP and Philippine asset traders, this carries multiple implications. A stronger yen and stabilized JGB market could reduce global risk-off pressure, offering modest relief to Asian EM currencies including the PHP. However, if US Treasury yields remain elevated or rise further despite intervention, this continues to present a headwind for PHP/USD, Philippine government bond yields, and capital flows into the PSEi. Watch for follow-through intervention signals and the trajectory of UST 10-year yields as key external drivers for PHP positioning in the near term.

---

high.title: Weak Consumption, Public Spending Likely Weighed on Q2 Growth
high.summary:
Philippine GDP growth is forecast to have slowed sharply in Q2 2026, with Deutsche Bank Research projecting just 2.5% expansion and Fitch Solutions/BMI estimating 2.7% — both markedly below the 5.4% recorded in Q2 2025 and the 2.8% seen in the prior quarter. The primary drags appear to be tepid consumer spending and subdued government disbursements. For FX and rates traders, this is a critical macro signal: a fourth consecutive quarter of deceleration materially raises the probability that the BSP will lean further into an easing cycle to stimulate domestic demand, which could place renewed downward pressure on the PHP. Bond investors may view weaker growth as constructive for duration, as it supports lower policy rates and a potential rally in government bond yields. However, if weak growth is accompanied by sticky inflation or persistent current account deficits, the BSP may face a policy dilemma. Watch for the official PSA GDP release and any subsequent BSP commentary on growth-inflation trade-offs, as these will be the key near-term catalysts for PHP/USD direction and the yield curve.

---

medium.title: BSP Bills' Rate Edges Up as Bids Drop
medium.summary: The BSP's 28-day short-term securities saw a slight uptick in average yield at Friday's auction, accompanied by a notable drop in demand. Total tenders came in at P43.39 billion against the P40 billion on offer (auction was oversubscribed), but this was significantly below the P62.18 billion in bids received in the prior week — pushing the bid-to-cover ratio down sharply to 1.08x from 1.55x previously. The declining appetite for BSP bills is a meaningful liquidity signal: it suggests banks may be less eager to park excess funds at the BSP's short-term facility, potentially indicating shifting liquidity conditions or a preference for higher-yielding alternatives. For rate and FX traders, the marginally higher BSP bill yield — even if small — reinforces the narrative that monetary easing remains off the table in the near term, which is modestly supportive for the Peso.

medium.title: BPI Plans to Pilot Stablecoin Remittances in Fourth Quarter
medium.summary: Bank of the Philippine Islands (BPI), one of the country's largest banks, plans to pilot stablecoin-based remittance infrastructure in Q4 2026 through a partnership with global digital clearing house Meridian. BPI's President and CEO Jose Teodoro Limcaoco confirmed the initiative, noting that fiat currency conversion will still underpin transactions. While this is primarily a fintech/banking story, it carries medium-term relevance for OFW remittance flows — a critical structural pillar of PHP support. If stablecoin rails reduce remittance friction and costs, it could incrementally boost the volume and speed of remittance inflows into the Philippines, providing a modest long-term positive for PHP demand. Regulatory execution risk under BSP's digital asset framework remains a key variable to monitor.

medium.title: BSP to Crack Down on Online Lenders' Unfair Debt Collection Practices
medium.summary:
The BSP is preparing to enforce stricter regulations targeting predatory lending and abusive debt collection practices by online lending companies (OLCs) once its full regulatory oversight of the sector is formalized. BSP General Counsel Roberto Figueroa confirmed that issuing regulations on these issues will be a top priority during the transition period. While this is primarily a consumer protection and financial inclusion issue rather than a direct FX or rates mover, it reflects the BSP's ongoing expansion of its regulatory perimeter into fintech and digital lending — a medium-term structural positive for the stability and credibility of the Philippine financial system. International investors with exposure to Philippine banks and financial sector equities should note the potential compliance cost implications for digital lending platforms.

---

medium.title: BPI Expects Profit Rebound This Semester
medium.summary:
Bank of the Philippine Islands (BPI), one of the Philippines' largest listed banks and a major PSEi constituent, expects second-half profit growth to outpace the first half, driven by expansion in its corporate loan book offsetting weakness in consumer and SME lending segments. This guidance is relevant for PSEi watchers, as BPI's performance is a bellwether for the broader banking sector's health and the credit cycle. Pressure on consumer and small business lending may signal tightening credit conditions among retail borrowers, which warrants monitoring for broader macro implications. The H2 rebound expectation, if delivered, could provide positive support for banking sector equities on the PSEi.

---

medium.title: Philippine Manufacturing PMI Hits 5-Month High in July
medium.summary: The S&P Global Philippines Manufacturing PMI rose to 51.8 in July from 50.9 in June, marking the highest reading in five months and the third consecutive month of expansion. Production and new orders grew at their fastest pace since February, signaling broadening domestic economic momentum. For FX and bond investors, improving manufacturing activity reinforces the case for sustained GDP growth, which could support BSP's willingness to hold rates steady or proceed cautiously with further easing. A resilient growth backdrop is modestly supportive of PHP and could temper aggressive bearish positioning on Philippine assets.

medium.title: World Bank Keeps 2026 Philippine Growth Forecast Unchanged
medium.summary: The World Bank maintained its 2026 Philippine GDP growth forecast at 3.7%, within the government's 3.5%–4.5% target range, but trimmed its 2027 projection to 5.2% from 5.6% previously, citing lingering external risks expected to weigh on activity into next year. The downward revision to 2027 reflects caution around global headwinds — a relevant signal for medium-term capital flow and bond demand dynamics. While the unchanged 2026 forecast provides near-term stability for sentiment on Philippine assets, the downgraded outer-year outlook may give international fund managers pause on longer-duration Philippine government bonds and equity multiple expansion. Monitor whether the BSP adjusts its own growth and inflation projections in response to the World Bank's revised assessment.

medium.title: DoF Proposes Higher Excise Taxes
medium.summary: The Department of Finance is proposing new and higher excise taxes on sweetened beverages, e-cigarettes, flexible plastics, luxury vehicles, and private aircraft under its PROGRESS bill, aimed at offsetting revenue losses from proposed personal income tax cuts. While primarily a fiscal policy story, the revenue implications are relevant for bond market participants — successful passage could improve the fiscal deficit trajectory, potentially supporting demand for Philippine Government Securities (PGS) and putting modest downward pressure on long-end yields. Conversely, the inflationary pass-through from higher excise taxes on consumer goods warrants monitoring given the BSP's inflation targeting mandate and its influence on the rate path.

medium.title: PHL Stocks End Higher on Peace Talks, Strong Data
medium.summary: The PSEi rebounded strongly on Monday, gaining 1.57% (+98.28 points) to close at 6,334.72, with the broader All Shares index also rising 1.03% to 3,430.16. Sentiment was lifted by easing Middle East geopolitical tensions — following statements by US President Trump on limiting further strikes — which dragged global oil prices lower, a net positive for the Philippines as an oil-importing economy. The manufacturing PMI expansion data (see below) also contributed to the risk-on tone. For equity and FX traders, the decline in oil prices is notable as it helps reduce the Philippines' import bill, easing pressure on the current account and offering modest PHP support at the margin. The PSEi recovery warrants monitoring to assess whether this represents a sustained re-rating or a short-term bounce driven by global risk sentiment.

medium.title: Philippines Manufacturing PMI Expands for a Third Straight Month in July
medium.summary: The S&P Global Philippines Manufacturing PMI rose to 51.8 in July from 50.9 in June, marking a third consecutive month of expansion and signaling a broadening recovery in factory activity. Stronger demand conditions were the primary driver, though rising input costs remain a point of caution. While the PMI reading is modestly positive for Philippine growth sentiment and provides some support for the PHP and equities, the caveat on input cost pressures is worth monitoring — if these feed through into consumer prices, they could complicate the BSP's inflation outlook and limit the scope for further rate cuts. The data served as a near-term catalyst for Monday's PSEi rally and may temper the most bearish Q2 GDP forecasts at the margin.
